title: I Let the Roommate Keep the Chore Wheel He Invented

parts.text: I spun the chore wheel and watched it land on me for the ninth time. I am twenty-three, first office job, shared kitchen at 2 a.m. My roommate Owen 3D-printed a wheel after I asked for fairness. The wheel was weighted. I checked with a phone level app. The bubble drifted every time toward TAKE OUT TRASH. The kitchen smelled like old garlic and his protein powder. Our third roommate, Sana, was at nights at the hospital. Owen said, "The wheel doesn't lie" I said, "The coin under it does" I photographed the bubble, then the underside, a coin taped near trash. Owen came in for a banana. The banana had brown spots, specific, ugly. I remember the cheap smell of the room, which is how I know I was there. social.description: 2 a.m. garlic kitchen, a 3D-printed wheel, and a phone level. Nine landings were not fate. Would you have peeled the coin off?

parts.text: I peeled the coin off in front of him and spun again. It landed on vacuum, his least favorite. Sana came home, looked at the coin, and started laughing in her scrubs. We made a spreadsheet instead, the ugly kind with dates. Owen called it corporate. I called it not a scam. He moved out at lease break and tried to take the air fryer we split. Sana had the Target receipt. He left the wheel. I keep it as art. The protein smell faded. Fairness, it turns out, is just dates. Sana said, "Is that a quarter taped to the plastic" Owen said, "It's for balance" The banana spots are a core memory, which is embarrassing. I still take the trash out on my actual days. That is the whole moral. I remember the cheap smell of the room, which is how I know I was there. I remember the cheap smell of the room, which is how I know I was there.
